question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative inverse of $3$ modulo $7,$ denoted ${3}^{-1},$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
3\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,7).
$$

Note that since $\text{gcd}(3,7)=1,$ an inverse element exists and is unique up to congruence modulo $7.$

Since the modulus $n=7$ is small, we can find the inverse $x$ by computing exponents of $3$ (modulo $7$) until we get a result of $1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{2} & ≡3\cdot 3≡9≡7+2≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ {3}^{3} & ≡3\cdot 2≡6 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ {3}^{4} & ≡3\cdot 6≡18≡2\cdot 7+4≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ {3}^{5} & ≡3\cdot 4≡12≡7+5≡5 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ {3}^{6} & ≡3\cdot 5≡15≡2\cdot 7+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $3\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,7).$ Therefore, the multiplicative inverse of $3$ modulo $7$ is $5.$
